preview.name: strip-ansi
preview.description:
Need the text without terminal styling? strip-ansi turns an ANSI-decorated string into plain text.

Import stripAnsi, then pass the string directly; the README’s underlined Unicorn example returns just “Unicorn.”

It also handles terminal hyperlinks: the documented link example keeps “Click” while removing its escape wrapper.

Already-clean text needs no special handling: tests expect “foo bar” and the empty string to remain unchanged.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body:
Inside index.js, the call first checks the input type; anything other than a string throws TypeError.

For decorated input, a regular expression created by ansi-regex supplies the matches, and replace removes them.

A test makes that outcome concrete: combined styling around “bar” is expected to produce “bar.”

sections.title: A closer look
sections.body:
The key shortcut is an early return when neither ESC nor the eight-bit CSI introducer appears.

The source also explains why it leaves regex state alone: replace resets lastIndex automatically.
